headline: Spanish Frequent Verbs Master
threshold: Recognize and use sixty frequent spoken verbs, their everyday meanings, complements and regional cautions.

lessons.title: Entering and joining in
lessons.objective: Entering and joining in: Entrar en or entrar a can introduce a place, with regional preferences.

words.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
Deje la mochila en el casillero.
words.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.
Do not touch the works of art.

words.es: Si vienen en grupo, esperen junto a la escalera.
words.en: If you come as a group, wait next to the stairs.

words.es: Pregunten al personal si necesitan ayuda.
words.en: Ask the staff if you need help.

words.es: Entré al museo con mi hermana.
words.en: I entered the museum with my sister.

words.es: Antes de entrar, mostramos los boletos.
words.en: Before entering, we showed the tickets.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing entering and joining in. Entrar en or entrar a can introduce a place, with regional preferences. Entrar is a regular -ar verb. Distinguish it from salir de when describing movement. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Entrar en or entrar a can introduce a place, with regional preferences. Entrar is a regular -ar verb. Distinguish it from salir de when describing movement.

examples.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
examples.en: Go through this door, please.

examples.es: Deje la mochila en el casillero.
examples.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.

lessons.title: Following and continuing
lessons.objective: Following and continuing: Seguir changes e to i in stressed present forms and uses sigo in yo; siguió in preterite.

words.en: Right now I am preparing a presentation.

words.es: Mis compañeros están leyendo los resultados.
words.en: My classmates are reading the results.

words.es: Ayer a esta hora estábamos buscando información.
words.en: Yesterday at this time we were looking for information.

words.es: Yo estaba escribiendo cuando se apagó la computadora.
words.en: I was writing when the computer turned off.

words.es: Hoy estamos guardando el trabajo con frecuencia.
words.en: Today we are saving the work frequently.

words.es: No estamos usando el equipo que falló ayer.
words.en: We are not using the equipment that failed yesterday.
We are still preparing the presentation.

words.es: El programa siguió funcionando después del reinicio.
words.en: The program continued working after the restart.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing following and continuing. Seguir changes e to i in stressed present forms and uses sigo in yo; siguió in preterite. Seguir + gerund means continue doing something. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Seguir changes e to i in stressed present forms and uses sigo in yo; siguió in preterite. Seguir + gerund means continue doing something.

examples.es: Ahora estoy preparando una presentación.
examples.en: Right now I am preparing a presentation.

examples.es: Mis compañeros están leyendo los resultados.
examples.en: My classmates are reading the results.

lessons.title: Searching without claiming a result
lessons.objective: Searching without claiming a result: Buscar means look for, not necessarily find.

words.es: Busco a la persona que organiza el curso.
words.en: I am looking for the person who organizes the course.

words.es: La mujer que está junto a la puerta es la coordinadora.
words.en: The woman who is next to the door is the coordinator.

words.es: Tengo una pregunta sobre el mensaje que recibí.
words.en: I have a question about the message I received.

words.es: El enlace que enviaron no funciona.
words.en: The link they sent does not work.

words.es: Ella me dio una dirección que sí funciona.
words.en: She gave me an address that does work.

words.es: Ahora puedo abrir el documento que necesito.
words.en: Now I can open the document I need.

words.es: Busco a la coordinadora del curso.
words.en: I am looking for the course coordinator.

words.es: Ayer busqué el enlace en todos mis mensajes.
words.en: Yesterday I looked for the link in all my messages.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing searching without claiming a result. Buscar means look for, not necessarily find. It takes a direct object; use personal a for a specific person. Yo preterite busqué preserves the sound. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Buscar means look for, not necessarily find. It takes a direct object; use personal a for a specific person. Yo preterite busqué preserves the sound.

examples.es: Busco a la persona que organiza el curso.
examples.en: I am looking for the person who organizes the course.

examples.es: La mujer que está junto a la puerta es la coordinadora.
examples.en: The woman who is next to the door is the coordinator.

lessons.title: Taking out and obtaining
lessons.objective: Taking out and obtaining: Sacar often means take out; sacar una foto means take a photo.

words.en: Do you have the hotel reservation?

words.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
words.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.
Where did you put the tickets?

words.es: Los puse dentro de la mochila.
words.en: I put them inside the backpack.

words.es: Necesito el pasaporte, pero no lo encuentro.
words.en: I need the passport, but I cannot find it.

words.es: Aquí está; lo dejaste sobre la mesa.
words.en: Here it is; you left it on the table.

words.es: Saqué los boletos de la mochila.
words.en: I took the tickets out of the backpack.

words.es: Saca también una copia de la reserva.
words.en: Take out a copy of the reservation too.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing taking out and obtaining. Sacar often means take out; sacar una foto means take a photo. Yo preterite saqué and subjunctive saque preserve the hard c sound. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Sacar often means take out; sacar una foto means take a photo. Yo preterite saqué and subjunctive saque preserve the hard c sound.

examples.es: ¿Tienes la reserva del hotel?
examples.en: Do you have the hotel reservation?

examples.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
examples.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.

lessons.title: Returning and doing again
lessons.objective: Returning and doing again: Volver a + infinitive means do again.

words.es: Cuando llegamos, la tienda ya había cerrado.
words.en: When we arrived, the store had already closed.

words.es: Yo había consultado un horario antiguo.
words.en: I had checked an old schedule.

words.es: Mi hermano había salido temprano del trabajo.
words.en: My brother had left work early.

words.es: Nadie nos había avisado del cambio.
words.en: Nobody had told us about the change.

words.es: Por suerte habíamos guardado el recibo.
words.en: Fortunately we had kept the receipt.

words.es: Volvimos al día siguiente para hacer el cambio.
words.en: We returned the next day to make the exchange.

words.es: Volvimos a la tienda al día siguiente.
words.en: We returned to the store the next day.

words.es: El empleado nos pidió volver a explicar el problema.
words.en: The employee asked us to explain the problem again.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing returning and doing again. Volver a + infinitive means do again. Present vuelvo changes o to ue; participle vuelto is irregular. Volver de names the place returned from. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Volver a + infinitive means do again. Present vuelvo changes o to ue; participle vuelto is irregular. Volver de names the place returned from.

examples.es: Cuando llegamos, la tienda ya había cerrado.
examples.en: When we arrived, the store had already closed.

examples.es: Yo había consultado un horario antiguo.
examples.en: I had checked an old schedule.

lessons.title: Purchases and recipients
lessons.objective: Purchases and recipients: Comprar is regular.

words.es: Voy a comprar un regalo para Luis.
words.en: I am going to buy a gift for Luis.

words.es: Lo voy a buscar en la tienda del centro.
words.en: I am going to look for it in the downtown store.
I prefer to buy it today.

words.es: Sí, te puedo acompañar después del trabajo.
words.en: Yes, I can go with you after work.

words.es: Queremos envolverlo antes de la fiesta.
words.en: We want to wrap it before the party.
I bought a scarf for Luis.

words.es: Normalmente compro los regalos con tiempo.
words.en: I normally buy gifts ahead of time.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing purchases and recipients. Comprar is regular. Comprar algo para alguien names the intended recipient; comprarle algo a alguien can identify the seller or recipient depending on context. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Comprar is regular. Comprar algo para alguien names the intended recipient; comprarle algo a alguien can identify the seller or recipient depending on context.

examples.es: Voy a comprar un regalo para Luis.
examples.en: I am going to buy a gift for Luis.

examples.es: Lo voy a buscar en la tienda del centro.
examples.en: I am going to look for it in the downtown store.

lessons.title: Payment and who receives it
lessons.objective: Payment and who receives it: Pagar is regular except spelling changes such as pagué / pague.

words.es: Este paquete es para mi hermana.
words.en: This package is for my sister.

words.es: Compré una caja para proteger el regalo.
words.en: I bought a box to protect the gift.

words.es: Pasé por la oficina de correos.
words.en: I went by the post office.

words.es: Pagué diez euros por el envío.
words.en: I paid ten euros for the shipping.

words.es: Gracias por ayudarme con la dirección.
words.en: Thank you for helping me with the address.
I paid for the shipping by card.

words.es: Mi hermana pagará la próxima compra.
words.en: My sister will pay for the next purchase.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing payment and who receives it. Pagar is regular except spelling changes such as pagué / pague. Pagar algo pays a bill; pagar por algo gives the thing exchanged for payment. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Pagar is regular except spelling changes such as pagué / pague. Pagar algo pays a bill; pagar por algo gives the thing exchanged for payment.

examples.es: Este paquete es para mi hermana.
examples.en: This package is for my sister.

examples.es: Lo necesito para el viernes.
examples.en: I need it by Friday.

lessons.title: Asking a question
lessons.objective: Asking a question: Preguntar asks for information; pedir asks for an item, action or favor.

words.es: Busco a la persona que organiza el curso.
words.en: I am looking for the person who organizes the course.

words.es: La mujer que está junto a la puerta es la coordinadora.
words.en: The woman who is next to the door is the coordinator.

words.es: Tengo una pregunta sobre el mensaje que recibí.
words.en: I have a question about the message I received.

words.es: El enlace que enviaron no funciona.
words.en: The link they sent does not work.

words.es: Ella me dio una dirección que sí funciona.
words.en: She gave me an address that does work.

words.es: Ahora puedo abrir el documento que necesito.
words.en: Now I can open the document I need.

words.es: Le pregunté a la coordinadora dónde estaba el formulario.
words.en: I asked the coordinator where the form was.

words.es: Ella me preguntó si tenía una copia del mensaje.
words.en: She asked me whether I had a copy of the message.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing asking a question. Preguntar asks for information; pedir asks for an item, action or favor. Preguntarle a alguien introduces the person asked; preguntar por can ask about someone. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Preguntar asks for information; pedir asks for an item, action or favor. Preguntarle a alguien introduces the person asked; preguntar por can ask about someone.

examples.es: Busco a la persona que organiza el curso.
examples.en: I am looking for the person who organizes the course.

examples.es: La mujer que está junto a la puerta es la coordinadora.
examples.en: The woman who is next to the door is the coordinator.

lessons.title: Taking, drinking and choosing transport
lessons.objective: Taking, drinking and choosing transport: Tomar has several everyday meanings.

words.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
words.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.
First I looked for the correct exit.
Then I bought a one-way ticket.

words.es: El tren salió a las ocho.
Llamé a Elena y expliqué el problema.
words.en: I called Elena and explained the problem.
In the end we took a bus.

words.es: Tomé un autobús después de perder el tren.
words.en: I took a bus after missing the train.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing taking, drinking and choosing transport. Tomar has several everyday meanings. Tomar el autobús means take the bus; tomar agua means drink water; tomar una decisión means make a decision. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Tomar has several everyday meanings. Tomar el autobús means take the bus; tomar agua means drink water; tomar una decisión means make a decision.

examples.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
examples.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.

examples.es: Primero busqué la salida correcta.
examples.en: First I looked for the correct exit.

lessons.title: Changing and exchanging
lessons.objective: Changing and exchanging: Cambiar algo changes an object; cambiar de shifts category or choice; cambiar algo por otra cosa exchanges one thing for another.

words.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
words.en: I would like to stay one more night.
Would you have a quieter room?

words.es: Yo pediría una que no dé a la calle.
words.en: I would ask for one that does not face the street.

words.es: Sería mejor confirmar el precio primero.
words.en: It would be better to confirm the price first.

words.es: La recepcionista dijo que revisaría las opciones.
words.en: The receptionist said she would review the options.

words.es: Quisiera cambiar la fecha de mi reserva.
words.en: I would like to change the date of my reservation.

words.es: El hotel cambió de encargado el mes pasado.
words.en: The hotel changed managers last month.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing changing and exchanging. Cambiar algo changes an object; cambiar de shifts category or choice; cambiar algo por otra cosa exchanges one thing for another. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Cambiar algo changes an object; cambiar de shifts category or choice; cambiar algo por otra cosa exchanges one thing for another.

examples.es: ¿Podría cambiar mi reserva?
examples.en: Could I change my reservation?

examples.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
examples.en: I would like to stay one more night.

lessons.title: Going up and raising
lessons.objective: Going up and raising: Subir can be intransitive go up or transitive raise / upload.

words.es: Mi primo pidió una habitación tranquila.
words.en: My cousin asked for a quiet room.

words.es: La recepcionista repitió el número del piso.
words.en: The receptionist repeated the floor number.

words.es: Mi primo durmió hasta las nueve.
Sus hijos durmieron un poco más.
words.en: His children slept a little longer.

words.es: Por la mañana todos pidieron agua.
words.en: In the morning everyone asked for water.

words.es: Subimos al cuarto piso con las maletas.
words.en: We went up to the fourth floor with the suitcases.
The elevator goes up very slowly.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing going up and raising. Subir can be intransitive go up or transitive raise / upload. Subir a names movement onto a vehicle or place; subir algo a internet names uploading. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Subir can be intransitive go up or transitive raise / upload. Subir a names movement onto a vehicle or place; subir algo a internet names uploading.

examples.es: Mi primo pidió una habitación tranquila.
examples.en: My cousin asked for a quiet room.

examples.es: La recepcionista repitió el número del piso.
examples.en: The receptionist repeated the floor number.

lessons.title: Losing, missing and getting lost
lessons.objective: Losing, missing and getting lost: Perder covers losing an object, losing a game or missing transport.

words.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
words.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.
First I looked for the correct exit.
Then I bought a one-way ticket.

words.es: El tren salió a las ocho.
Llamé a Elena y expliqué el problema.
words.en: I called Elena and explained the problem.
In the end we took a bus.

words.es: Perdí el tren por llegar tarde.
words.en: I missed the train because I arrived late.

words.es: Elena pensó que yo había perdido los boletos.
words.en: Elena thought I had lost the tickets.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing losing, missing and getting lost. Perder covers losing an object, losing a game or missing transport. Perderse means get lost. Present pierdo changes e to ie, but perdemos keeps e. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Perder covers losing an object, losing a game or missing transport. Perderse means get lost. Present pierdo changes e to ie, but perdemos keeps e.

examples.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
examples.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.

examples.es: Primero busqué la salida correcta.
examples.en: First I looked for the correct exit.

lessons.title: Waiting and hoping
lessons.objective: Waiting and hoping: Esperar a alguien means wait for a person.

words.es: Cuando llega un paquete, el portero nos llama.
words.en: When a package arrives, the doorman calls us.

words.es: Hoy estamos esperando una mesa nueva.
words.en: Today we are waiting for a new table.

words.es: Cuando llegue, voy a revisar la caja.
words.en: When it arrives, I am going to check the box.

words.es: En cuanto tengamos el recibo, te lo enviaré.
words.en: As soon as we have the receipt, I will send it to you.

words.es: No saldremos hasta que termine la entrega.
words.en: We will not leave until the delivery is finished.

words.es: Después de que revisemos todo, podremos salir.
words.en: After we check everything, we will be able to leave.

words.es: Esperamos la entrega desde las nueve.
words.en: We have been waiting for the delivery since nine.

words.es: Espero que la mesa llegue sin daños.
words.en: I hope the table arrives undamaged.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing waiting and hoping. Esperar a alguien means wait for a person. Esperar que commonly takes subjunctive when expressing a hope. Context distinguishes wait, expect and hope. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Esperar a alguien means wait for a person. Esperar que commonly takes subjunctive when expressing a hope. Context distinguishes wait, expect and hope.

examples.es: Cuando llega un paquete, el portero nos llama.
examples.en: When a package arrives, the doorman calls us.

examples.es: Hoy estamos esperando una mesa nueva.
examples.en: Today we are waiting for a new table.

lessons.title: Putting, throwing and fixed phrases
lessons.objective: Putting, throwing and fixed phrases: Echar has many contextual meanings.

words.es: Hay demasiada sal en la sopa.
words.en: There is too much salt in the soup.
There are still quite a few tomatoes left.

words.es: Necesitamos mucha agua para la pasta.
words.en: We need a lot of water for the pasta.
We cooked quite a lot, but we ate little.

words.es: Eché demasiada sal en la sopa.
words.en: I put too much salt in the soup.

words.es: Mi hermana echó un poco más de agua.
words.en: My sister added a little more water.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing putting, throwing and fixed phrases. Echar has many contextual meanings. Echar sal adds salt; echar de menos means miss someone; echar un vistazo means take a look. Do not apply one English gloss everywhere. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Echar has many contextual meanings. Echar sal adds salt; echar de menos means miss someone; echar un vistazo means take a look. Do not apply one English gloss everywhere.

examples.es: Hay demasiada sal en la sopa.
examples.en: There is too much salt in the soup.

examples.es: Tenemos pocas verduras frescas.
examples.en: We have few fresh vegetables.

lessons.title: Agreeing versus remembering
lessons.objective: Agreeing versus remembering: Acordar means agree or decide, usually with a direct object or infinitive.

words.es: Explicó que había llamado al médico.
words.en: She explained that she had called the doctor.

words.es: Nos contó que no podría venir a la reunión.
words.en: She told us that she would not be able to come to the meeting.

words.es: También dijo que enviaría sus notas.
words.en: She also said that she would send her notes.

words.es: Yo le respondí que podíamos esperar.
words.en: I replied that we could wait.

words.es: Quedamos en hablar de nuevo al día siguiente.
words.en: We agreed to talk again the next day.

words.es: Acordamos cambiar la fecha de la reunión.
words.en: We agreed to change the meeting date.

words.es: La coordinadora acordó el nuevo horario con Ana.
words.en: The coordinator agreed on the new schedule with Ana.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing agreeing versus remembering. Acordar means agree or decide, usually with a direct object or infinitive. Acordarse de means remember; both change o to ue in stressed present forms. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Acordar means agree or decide, usually with a direct object or infinitive. Acordarse de means remember; both change o to ue in stressed present forms.

examples.es: Ana dijo que estaba enferma.
examples.en: Ana said she was ill.

examples.es: Explicó que había llamado al médico.
examples.en: She explained that she had called the doctor.

lessons.title: Winning and earning
lessons.objective: Winning and earning: Ganar can mean win or earn.

words.es: Primero hablemos de la fecha de entrega.
words.en: First let us talk about the deadline.

words.es: Escribamos las tareas en esta hoja.
words.en: Let us write the tasks on this sheet.

words.es: No dejemos todo para el último día.
words.en: Let us not leave everything until the last day.

words.es: Revisemos el borrador juntos el jueves.
words.en: Let us review the draft together on Thursday.

words.es: Terminemos la reunión y vámonos a clase.
words.en: Let us finish the meeting and go to class.

words.es: Nuestro grupo ganó el concurso de proyectos.
words.en: Our group won the project competition.

words.es: Cada participante ganó una entrada para el museo.
words.en: Each participant won a ticket to the museum.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing winning and earning. Ganar can mean win or earn. Ganarle a alguien can mean beat someone. Ganarse la confianza means earn trust; the context determines the meaning. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Ganar can mean win or earn. Ganarle a alguien can mean beat someone. Ganarse la confianza means earn trust; the context determines the meaning.

examples.es: Vamos a dividir el trabajo.
examples.en: Let us divide the work.

examples.es: Primero hablemos de la fecha de entrega.
examples.en: First let us talk about the deadline.

lessons.title: Bringing toward a reference point
lessons.objective: Bringing toward a reference point: Traer means bring toward the speaker or reference point, compared with llevar away.

words.es: Ven a mi casa a las nueve.
words.en: Come to my house at nine.

words.es: Trae una caja pequeña si tienes.
words.en: Bring a small box if you have one.

words.es: Pon los libros junto a la puerta.
words.en: Put the books next to the door.

words.es: Haz una lista de las cosas frágiles.
words.en: Make a list of the fragile things.

words.es: Después llama a Julia y dile que ya estamos listos.
words.en: Then call Julia and tell her that we are ready.

words.es: Traje tres cajas para los libros.
words.en: I brought three boxes for the books.

words.es: Mi amiga trae papel para envolver la lámpara.
words.en: My friend is bringing paper to wrap the lamp.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing bringing toward a reference point. Traer means bring toward the speaker or reference point, compared with llevar away. Present traigo, preterite traje and participle traído need attention. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Traer means bring toward the speaker or reference point, compared with llevar away. Present traigo, preterite traje and participle traído need attention.

examples.es: Ven a mi casa a las nueve.
examples.en: Come to my house at nine.

examples.es: Trae una caja pequeña si tienes.
examples.en: Bring a small box if you have one.

lessons.title: Opening and available hours
lessons.objective: Opening and available hours: Abrir is regular in the present and preterite but has irregular participle abierto.

words.es: He abierto la sala de reuniones.
words.en: I have opened the meeting room.

words.es: Ana ha puesto las carpetas sobre la mesa.
words.en: Ana has put the folders on the table.

words.es: El director ha dicho que llegará a las diez.
words.en: The director has said that he will arrive at ten.
Have you seen the new document?

words.es: Sí, y hemos hecho una copia para cada persona.
words.en: Yes, and we have made a copy for each person.

words.es: Abrí la sala antes de que llegaran mis compañeros.
words.en: I opened the room before my coworkers arrived.

words.es: Normalmente la recepción abre a las ocho.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing opening and available hours. Abrir is regular in the present and preterite but has irregular participle abierto. Estar abierto describes a state; haber abierto describes a completed action. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Abrir is regular in the present and preterite but has irregular participle abierto. Estar abierto describes a state; haber abierto describes a completed action.

examples.en: I have opened the meeting room.

examples.es: Ana ha puesto las carpetas sobre la mesa.
examples.en: Ana has put the folders on the table.

lessons.title: Sending and giving orders
lessons.objective: Sending and giving orders: Mandar can send something or order an action.

words.es: Le escribí a Rosa esta mañana.
words.en: I wrote to Rosa this morning.

words.es: Le expliqué el cambio de horario.
words.en: I explained the schedule change to her.

words.es: Nos mandó la dirección del nuevo local.
words.en: She sent us the address of the new venue.
Did you let the others know?

words.es: Sí, les envié un mensaje a todos.
words.en: Yes, I sent a message to all of them.

words.es: Rosa nos mandó la dirección por mensaje.
words.en: Rosa sent us the address by message.

words.es: El director mandó revisar el enlace.
words.en: The director ordered the link to be checked.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing sending and giving orders. Mandar can send something or order an action. Mandar a alguien a un lugar sends a person there; a command may sound stronger than pedir. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Mandar can send something or order an action. Mandar a alguien a un lugar sends a person there; a command may sound stronger than pedir.

examples.es: Le escribí a Rosa esta mañana.
examples.en: I wrote to Rosa this morning.

examples.es: Le expliqué el cambio de horario.
examples.en: I explained the schedule change to her.

lessons.title: Remembering and reminding
lessons.objective: Remembering and reminding: Recordar algo means remember something; recordarle algo a alguien means remind someone.

words.en: We used to live near the river.

words.es: Nuestra casa tenía un patio pequeño.
words.en: Our house had a small courtyard.
My grandmother looked after the plants.

words.es: Yo iba a la escuela a pie.
words.en: I used to walk to school.

words.es: Desde la ventana veíamos las montañas.
words.en: From the window we could see the mountains.

words.es: Recuerdo el patio de nuestra antigua casa.
words.en: I remember the courtyard of our old house.

words.es: Mi abuela recordaba los nombres de todos los vecinos.
words.en: My grandmother remembered all the neighbors' names.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing remembering and reminding. Recordar algo means remember something; recordarle algo a alguien means remind someone. Unlike acordarse de, recordar normally takes no de before its direct object. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Recordar algo means remember something; recordarle algo a alguien means remind someone. Unlike acordarse de, recordar normally takes no de before its direct object.

examples.es: Antes vivíamos cerca del río.
examples.en: We used to live near the river.

examples.es: Nuestra casa tenía un patio pequeño.
examples.en: Our house had a small courtyard.
